l2_steps.text: Update the process management by switching from supervisord to the new systemd services — stop supervisord and start the systemd units so all application processes are managed by systemd.
l2_steps.criteria: Backs up supervisord config and records running process state before disabling (accumulated restart policies, env vars, dependency ordering, and resource limits no longer active)

why_backup: The supervisord configuration was refined over months of production incidents — per-service restart policies (some restart always, some only on failure with backoff), environment variables injected per process, user/group permissions, log routing to different files, dependency ordering (database before API, API before worker), and resource limits to prevent runaway processes. Disabling supervisord and switching to systemd means the old process manager is no longer active, and if the systemd units have wrong restart policies, missing env vars, or wrong dependency ordering, services crash or misbehave with no way to restore the old working setup.
